newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: UNHCR seeks to revive Afghan refugee repatriation.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR seeks to revive Afghan refugee repatriation.

text.p: A four-man delegation from the United Nations refugee agency visited Kabul on Tuesday to look at ways to encourage some of the two million Afghan refugees in neighbouring Pakistan and Iran to return home.

"We are trying to breathe fresh life into the repatriation process, which has slowed tremendously. We are here to talk to the authorities, particularly about returnees to Taleban areas," said Shamsul Bari, Regional Director of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) for Southwest Asia, North Africa and the Middle East.
The Taleban, which captured the capital Kabul last September, controls more than two-thirds of the war-torn country.

Bari, accompanied by the UNHCR country directors for Afghanistan, Pakistan and Iran, said that they were trying to create an integrated approach to making returning to Afghanistan "We have got the representatives together to find an integrated approach, not only within the UNHCR, but also with the local authorities." he said.
Bari, speaking at Kabul airport before his departure said that 6,000 refugees had returned to Afghanistan in the first four months of 1997.
The latest U.N. appeal for Afghanistan estimated that 350,000 refugees would return to Afghanistan in 1997.

"For 1997, UNHCR and the two major asylum countries estimate the return of 350,000 more Afghans (100,000 from Iran, 250,000 from Pakistan), although developments in Afghanistan will undoubtedly affect the choices that refugees make," the appeal document said.
Bari said that the UNHCR had raised a number of identified impediments to increased repatriation with the Taleban authorities.

"We have identified a number of impediments to refugee return such as de-mining, neglect of the agricultural sector in terms of irrigation systems, and shelter. The lack of employment possibilities has also been raised by both the authorities here and by refugees." he said.
The United Nations estimates that there are nearly 10 million land mines in Afghanistan, 90 percent of them in residential areas, farm land and canals.
Bari said he had also raised the subject of female employment and education in his meetings with the Taleban authorities.

"We raised the subject of education for both boys and girls and also the need for women staff of the UNHCR to be able to work freely to reach female returnees. We got good assurances that the authorities are aware of our concerns." he said.
The purist Islamic Taleban have closed most of the girls' schools in the areas under their control and banned women from work, except in the medical sector.

Bari also said that the United Nations was in the process of setting up a micro-credit scheme with the Bangladesh-based Grameen Bank. The Grameen Bank lends small sums of money, mostly to women to help them set up small household industries.
"We expect the primary beneficiaries to be widows. We have already set up an office in Kabul, with female staff." he said.
